title: Editor vs server content
when_to_use: Create/edit pages or posts; unsure whether to use block editor tools or server create/update-post.
principles: Trust page context: if is_block_editor=true, edit THIS open document with ahentic-browser/* — do not ahentic/create-post unless the user wants a separate post/page.
Do not call ahentic-browser/save-post after canvas edits unless the user explicitly asks to save, publish, or persist — Gutenberg keeps unsaved edits.
When the editor is NOT open: use ahentic/create-post / update-post / set-post-status (HITL for status).
Copy clientId values character-for-character from get-blocks / get-selection — never invent or recombine UUIDs.
For core/* text blocks, edit attributes directly; use get-block-type for third-party or after an attribute update fails.
If update/replace/insert returns ok:true, reply — do not re-fetch blocks only to verify unless the tool failed or the user asked to confirm.
steps: Read attached page context (or get-editor-state / get-current-page if URL looks like post.php / post-new.php / site-editor).
Editor open + build/edit request → update-post-title if needed, then insert-blocks / replace-blocks / update-block-attributes.
Editor closed + new content → create-post (draft-first) or update-post by id; publish only via set-post-status with HITL when asked.
User says save/publish while editor open → save-post and/or set-post-status as appropriate with HITL.
Ambiguous “create a contact page” while editing another draft → ask_user only if both intents are plausible; otherwise prefer editing the open doc when they said “this page” / “here”.
anti_patterns: ahentic/create-post while the block editor is open for the page they mean to fill.
save-post as a default last step after insert-blocks.
Guessing clientIds instead of copying from tool results.
Calling get-block-type first for every core/heading or core/paragraph edit.
